title: Wedding in Crete Guide to Seasons, Venues and Costs
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
notes: NEW guide (not a refresh). Broad Crete planning page above two drafts: content/posts/crete-wedding-venues (15 venues) and content/posts/greece-wedding-packages. Title promises 'Costs' but the person's standing rule is NO prices or amounts: the costs section covers WHAT DRIVES THE COST with no figures (season, guest numbers and rooms, exclusive use, venue fee vs package, extras priced separately, transfers, documents), from venue terms already sourced. Title kept as given.

OVERLAP: the Crete venues guide (draft) owns 'crete wedding venues'; this guide's venues section is short (east vs west, venue types, 5 to 6 named examples with one line each) and links the venues guide prominently. No repeated venue entries. The packages guide owns package detail; the costs section links it. SEO checks whether any site page ranks for 'wedding in crete' and variants (crete wedding, getting married in crete, crete wedding cost, best time to get married in crete, crete wedding season) and recommends the split with the venues guide.

AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Customs without a strong source are written as living practice in a confident voice ('Many couples...'), never with a meaning or origin stated as fact. 'Often told' at most once per post, never 'it is often told that'. No hedge stacking: cite a source once by link; date legal and travel facts once per section. Source gaps go in the run report only. No per-line source credits (never 'Britannica describes', 'the museum holds', 'the study records'). No myth-busting lines ('you will often read', 'confident dates').

Facts: reuse and re-check the facts in content/posts/crete-wedding-venues/03-source-pack.json and content/posts/greece-wedding-packages/03-source-pack.json (airports, east vs west, venue season windows and ceremony times, Smartraveller heat and wildfire, cost drivers from venue terms, Embassy Athens, Elounda Collection document steps and 40-day registration). New: seasons and weather from official sources only (Hellenic National Meteorological Service hnms.gr climate data, meteo.gr National Observatory of Athens, visitgreece.gr, incrediblecrete.gr).

Sections: why Crete (short); when to marry (seasons month by month from official sources and venue-stated windows); choosing an area and a venue (short, link the venues guide); what drives the cost (no figures, questions to ask, link the packages guide); getting there and getting around; legal in brief (as at November 2026, link the Greece guide legal section); a planning timeline (document lead times only as sourced); FAQ.

Sources: official tourism, meteorological and government sources, venues' own pages, Smartraveller, the Australian Embassy Athens. Never competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia.
Images: placeholders only; venue images licensed or press kit with permission only; never AI for a venue, destination or wedding; competitor images reference-only.

Speed: Apify web-fetch and DataForSEO. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: seasons and weather from official sources, island facts, airports re-checked, fact_01+; B: re-check cost-driver, legal and venue season facts from the two packs, fact_100+), 12 min HARD by the clock, no new reads after the limit, save after every 3 facts, scratch folders wic_a/wic_b; self_qa.confidence a number; must_include_coverage objects with covered_by arrays; never retry a declined call.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md; nothing on legal, church or religious paperwork; no transfer arrangements; no Wedded Privileges.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; venue names allowed as examples, no other vendor names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
